# GMEOW Deception Module

The GMEOW Deception Module — classes, properties, and individuals of the GMEOW super-vocabulary.

**IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/deception>  
**CURIE:** `gmeow:slices/deception`  

**Type:** `owl:Ontology`  

Cross-cutting deception, falsehood, and misinformation facility. Builds on the standpoint module (#43) and the event module (#41) to model deceptive acts as standpoint-indexed divergences between what a party holds true and what they project. Part of the Deception EPIC (#212).

DOCTRINE.
  * No isFalse / isDeceptive axiom and no boolean truth datatype property (Principles 1, 12). A falsehood is a frame-relative gmeow:StandpointClaim whose claimModality = gmeow:refuted (settled-false per a designated reference frame). Deceptiveness is asserted as a standpoint-indexed, attributed, confidence-weighted claim that coexists with its denial (Principle 9).
  * A deception is the divergence held-standpoint ≠ projected-standpoint, both modelled as ordinary StandpointClaims; the gap is the act, not a truth verdict.
  * Deception kind is an open gmeow:eventType value, never a subclass (events.ttl doctrine).
  * Intent is kept OUT of the logic: gmeow:deceptiveIntentClaim is a StandpointClaim (attributed/defeasible — vantage = assessor, wasAttributedTo, confidence).
  * Self-deception is a structural configuration: roleDeceiver = roleDeceived, avowed vs tacit sub-vantage.
  * The licensed-falsehood safety property (fiction, satire, sarcasm) is modelled via gmeow:veridicalityLicensedFalsehood, keeping these forms distinct from deception.
  * DL-clean by construction (Principle 3): all new properties are simple ObjectProperties, no transitivity/chain/inverse axioms.

**Defined by:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/slices/deception>
